subject: Financial exposure framing & SLA escape hatch
content:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Liability exposure framing for Nimbus — cap options

Team,

Quick summary from last night's call with Nimbus (Alyssa & contracts team): they're asking for an exceptions carveout for data-processing failures that cause regulatory fines, and they want a cap aligned with annual fees rather than total contract value. They also pushed hard against consequential damages carveouts — they'd like a broad carveout for certain downstream hospital reimbursement losses tied to our inference outputs.

What I promised to surface: (1) practical cap constructs we can live with for a SMBA/POC customer (they're starting with a 12-mo SOW); (2) an explanation of why annualized fee multiples are preferable for us vs. cumulative contract cap; (3) a suggested SLA escape hatch language we can offer to limit short-term operational exposure while we onboard.

Attachments: draft MSA (v3 redline) and SOW estimate from tonight's update.

Next steps: Marissa/Steph — can you sketch 3 practical options (a, b, c) that we can run by Alyssa next week:
- Option A: Flat multiple of annual fees (2x annual fees) + enumerated carveouts for gross negligence & IP infringement only.
- Option B: Cumulative cap (contract term) at 1.5x total fees with a limited regulatory fines carveout up to $250k.
- Option C: Annual rolling cap per 12-mo billing window equal to fees collected in that window (with renewal reset) + explicit carveouts for SOC2-adjacent regulatory penalties but excluding consequential damages.

Please include a short operational note on how each option would affect escrow/credits, and whether the SLA escape hatch (temporary throttling/failover to hosted fallback) can be invoked without triggering a material breach.

Thanks — Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Liability exposure framing for Nimbus — cap options

Jonas —

Thanks for the write-up. High level comments and then I'll follow with markup in the attached doc: 

1) Terminology: we should avoid "consequential damages" ambiguity by proposing a narrow definition for both parties. For Nimbus's use case (clinical decision support), the risk is high but the causal chain is long; we can offer to carve out a limited subset (direct patient-safety related damages) but we need to cap that separately.

2) Annualized vs. contract aggregate: annualized caps are cleaner operationally (billing aligns and we can reconcile per-invoice), but they increase our aggregate exposure over a multi-year term. If Nimbus insists on annual reset, propose a higher per-year multiple (e.g., 2.5x annual fees) to compensate.

3) Regulatory fines carveout: we can agree to a regulatory-fines carveout only where fines directly result from Redwood's breach of our security obligations (e.g., failure to apply agreed encryption or data-segregation). We should explicitly exclude fines arising from customer's failure to follow operational protocols.

4) SLA escape hatch: propose limited-scope operational controls (rate limiting, temporary model downgrade, mandatory throttle for high-risk endpoints) that are available as remedies but tagged as non-material for termination purposes if used in good faith. That reduces termination risk.

I'll upload a redline that implements: Option A as our baseline (2x annual fees), Option B as a procurement-constrained counter, Option C as a commercial concession with higher annual multiple + more granular carveouts. Also adding a short note on credit/retention mechanics.

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: [attachment: Redwood_MSA_v3_redline.docx]

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@nimbushealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, contracts@nimbushealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Mar 2028 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Liability exposure framing for Nimbus — cap options

Jonas / Marissa —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the options. A few points from our side after internal review: 

- Annual reset is our preference operationally — it makes budgeting and insurance alignment far simpler for us. If Redwood requires a higher multiple for an annual reset, we need a concrete rationale on how the multiple was derived.
- Our legal team will not accept a carveout that lets Redwood avoid responsibility for downstream reimbursement losses that are a direct consequence of an incorrect inference in a high-risk triage workflow. We are willing to cap those but would prefer a formula tied to a rolling 12-mo revenue at hospital unit level rather than a flat $ amount.
- Regarding regulatory fines: we accept your proposal to limit to failures tied to Redwood's security obligations, but we need the MSA to include a mandatory incident response SLA and transparent forensic reporting so we can demonstrate good faith to regulators.

We'll be on a decision call Thursday — can Marissa provide the three options with a short rationale and a recommended fallback? Also please confirm whether the SLA escape hatch can be used while we run a rolling canary without it being treated as a breach.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Partnerships
Nimbus Health

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@nimbushealth.com>, contracts@nimbushealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Mar 2028 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Liability exposure framing for Nimbus — cap options

Alyssa —

Thanks — noted. Marissa will send the three-option memo by Tuesday COB with a short rationale for the multiplier math and operational notes on invoking the SLA escape hatch. Two clarifications up front so we come to Thursday's call with an aligned set of redlines: 

1) Can you confirm whether Nimbus prefers a per-invoice reconciliation cadence (monthly) versus an annual true-up for the annual-cap construct? That affects how we model credits/usage-based revenue recognition.

2) For the downstream reimbursement exposure: if you can provide a simple sample calculation (e.g., revenue loss tie-out for an illustrative hospital unit), it would help us model a defensible limit rather than purely open-ended exposure.

We want to be reasonable here — the goal is to get Nimbus comfortable while keeping Redwood's aggregate enterprise risk predictable for finance and insurance.

I'll include the redline and a commercial note from Priyom on proposed premium/credit adjustments for each option.

Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
